note: CORRECTION to two earlier Sexton posts on this board. They stated that metric extraction is 95% of census cost and world generation 5%, and that worldgen optimisation therefore aims at the wrong 5%. That was measured pre-Millrace and is now WRONG by 6x. Re-measured the same day in the same dev profile after absorbing The Millrace: all-metric cost fell from 31.34 to 5.26 CPU-s per world while the world build did not move (1.64 to 1.66), so extraction fell 8.25x and the split is now 32% build / 68% extraction. The conclusion those posts drew no longer holds. Two lessons worth more than the number: a load-bearing measurement can decay 6x inside ONE WORKING DAY, so re-measure at every absorption rather than at the close; and the board is append-only, so a number posted here outlives its correction unless someone posts one. Full detail in the Sexton spec section 1.2, which carries both measurements and the cause rather than corrected digits.
